title: jCodeMunch evidence receipt
description: An immutable evidence receipt (jcodemunch.evidence/v1, #377 phase 2), served at munch://evidence/<evidence_id>. Records what exact evidence a reference proves, against what snapshot, produced by what operation. The server attests; it never concludes. Whether a receipt SATISFIES a claim's declared needs is Phase 4 and is deliberately not modelled here.

evidence_id.description: sha256 over the canonical (subject, effective_search, snapshot) payload. Different snapshot means a different id. Always the FULL digest: 48 bits of displayed identity is a birthday problem waiting for a large session. Rendered prose may show a short prefix; identity, comparison and storage never do.

proof_kind.description: What this receipt is a proof OF. A producer may mint only the kinds its operation supports (evidence/producers.py). The document_* and column_* kinds are the jdocmunch and jdatamunch halves of the suite vocabulary, named here so parity attaches to one enum rather than inventing a second.

product.description: The suite member that minted this receipt.

subject.description: The exact thing this receipt proves something about — the Phase 1 caveat closed. Read from the SERVED row only, never re-read from the index: a receipt describes what the caller was handed. Fields the response did not carry are OMITTED and named in limitations rather than quietly filled in.

repo_identity.description: RESOLVED repo identity, not the caller's argument string: '.', an alias, a path and a worktree can all name one repo.

content_sha256.description: Hash of the symbol body. With a line range, a file-level citation stops being indistinguishable from a symbol-level one.

query.description: Absence receipts only: the query whose absence was scanned for.

effective_search.description: A descriptor of the operation that ACTUALLY ran, emitted by the producer's canonical projector — not the raw caller arguments, and not the finalizer reverse-engineering semantics from them. Absent and empty-valued keys are dropped so kind=null cannot mint a different id from an omitted kind.

scope.description: Arguments that NARROWED what was searched. 'Not found' means nothing without the scope it was not found in.

mode.description: Arguments and observed conditions that changed WHICH operation ran (ranking mode, channels, thresholds, whether the implicit fuzzy pass fired). A literal search and a regex search of one string are different operations and must not collide on one id.

scope.description: A read-only view of effective_search.scope, kept beside it so a reader does not have to reconstruct it. NOT a separate identity input — everything in it is already inside effective_search.

snapshot.description: What this receipt was measured against. Phase 2 BINDS these; every field already shipped (subject_state.capture, FreshnessProbe.repo_freshness v1.108.180, index_coverage_meta v1.108.176, verdict.working_tree v1.108.181).

freshness.description: Four-state, never a boolean: 'I could not find out' has its own value. channels.index also carries 'rebuilding' and 'partial', which are corpus conditions rather than freshness values; they stay in channels and are named in limitations rather than collapsing into a freshness word.

working_tree.description: Measured only for a zero-result scan, so a positive receipt reports 'unknown' — which is what it is, not 'clean'.

coverage_fingerprint.description: OPAQUE digest of the coverage block. Deliberately not a corpus manifest: source-universe identity, per-file parse outcomes and parser capability fingerprints are Phase 5 (#385). What it buys today is that two otherwise-identical scans over corpora with different coverage cannot share an evidence id.

conditions.description: Sorted tokens for the conditions this response was produced under. Inside the identity payload on purpose, twice over: a subject measured under different conditions gets a different evidence id (which is what 'different snapshot, different id' has to mean when the conditions are what changed), and every entry in `limitations` is derived from a token here, so two receipts sharing an id necessarily carry the same body. Without that, a cached replay whose verdict gained `revalidated` would produce one id with two different bodies, and the fail-closed collision check would delete a receipt an agent was already holding.

channels.description: The verdict channel block this receipt was minted from, verbatim. Same vocabulary as retrieval-verdict.schema.json.

coverage.description: The coverage contract at scan time, or null when the index predates coverage recording. Null means coverage UNKNOWN, never 'nothing was excluded'.

integrity.description: What, if anything, this receipt can attest about bytes rather than identity.

hash_source.description: index_content_hash = the hash the index stored for the full body. served_bytes = hashed from the body this response actually carried.

scanned.description: Absence receipts: the scan counts backing the claim.

capabilities.description: What this receipt can support, made legible so Phase 4 can match a claim's declared requirements against it. Phase 2 does not judge them. proves_absence is ADVISORY: finalization re-derives it from the linked scan record via handoff.absence_refusal, so there is exactly one implementation of the refusal rules and a receipt read hours later cannot disagree with the gate that issued it.

limitations.description: What this receipt CANNOT prove. The field that makes a weak receipt usable rather than discardable: a receipt that knows its own limits is worth more than one that omits them.

absence_ref.description: Absence receipts: the Phase 3 token (v1.108.166) naming the recorded scan this receipt points at. The link is what keeps handoff.absence_refusal the single implementation of the refusal rules, and it is why a Phase 3 ref a shipped agent is already holding keeps working.
